verdictStatement.summary: v11 is a large, real advance and I say so first, because most of what it claims I reproduced by execution and could not break. Its diagnosis of v10 is exactly right and I reproduced it: AX2 rebuilt against check-evaluation-proof-v10.py exits 0 with v10's complete green banner including 'ROUTING ESTABLISHED BEHAVIOURALLY ... 0 served by the superseded module (REQUIRED zero)' while 7 of 7 pinned vectors' verdicts are produced by check-c2.py. Its central novelty is also real and measured exactly as published: A-1 value equality agrees 21/21 for joins that return check-c2.py's answer (AX2 and AX3), and A-2's PRIVATE witness is the only rule that catches AX8 — I measured AX8 at A-1 21/21, A-3 21/21, A-4 21/21, A-5 7/7 and the SHARED ledger 21/21, with A-2 alone at 14/21. The preserved v10 measurements reproduce by execution digit for digit; the two silent-accept enumerations reproduce position for position under my own walker and my own direct drives; 27 of 27 pins agree; non-circularity is exact; --selftest is 36/36 with a distinct 0/1/2/3 matrix; there are no paper seals. BUT the load-bearing property does not hold. A-2 tags a returned object by WHICH MODULE OBJECT THE ATTRIBUTE WAS FOUND ON, not by which pinned bytes computed it, and _witnessing reads that attribute at window entry. A route region using ONLY the two arguments it is handed — no sys, no frames, no getattr, nothing the introspection tripwire names — can install its own serving function on authority.c2v4()'s attribute, wrapped by the ledger's OWN _wrap under the repaired tag. Every rule then holds by construction: call provenance 28/21/0, A-1 21/21, A-2 21/21, A-3 21/21, A-4 21/21, A-5 7/7, oracle 0 mismatches. MEASURED: evasion_rx1.py exits 0 with the complete green banner including 'ANSWER PROVENANCE ESTABLISHED ... 21 ARE the object that module produced for this vector (A-2)', --selftest returns SELFTEST-PASS with all 36 mutations rejected and no variant escaping, every published number reproduces unchanged, and 7 of 7 pinned vectors' validation verdicts are produced by check-c2.py and 0 of 7 by check-c2-v4.py. That is the IR-EP10-01 class, in the repair built to close it, with the new guard green. Separately I defeated the introspection tripwire — the SOLE guard for the class RES-EP11-02 concedes — with a spelling it does not enumerate, and that variant also exits 0 green with 7/7 answered by check-c2.py.

blockers.title: A-2 does not establish answer provenance: the private witness tags an object by WHICH MODULE OBJECT the attribute was found on, so a route region that installs its own serving function on authority.c2v4()'s attribute satisfies all five rules while 7/7 pinned verdicts come from check-c2.py — with no introspection of any kind
blockers.statement: evaluation-proof.v11.json answerProvenance.property claims 'for every pinned vector, each value the join returns and the checker acts on — the validation verdict above all, plus the commitment and the canonical preimage — is the value the repaired module produced for that PlanIntent', with isSoleGuardForAnswerProvenance=true and establishesCallProvenanceOnly=false. The mechanism cannot support that. _witnessing(witness, tagged) reads `getattr(module, api)` at window entry and installs a wrapper that records `(tag, api, argfp, depth, result)` where `tag` is fixed by WHICH MODULE OBJECT the attribute was read from — not by which pinned bytes computed the result. A-2 then asks only that the returned object be one the witness recorded against C2V4. So A-2 establishes 'this object came out of whatever function was bound at check-c2-v4.py's module attribute at the moment the guard looked', which the route region controls. EVASION RX1, mine, not among the nineteen: on its first call c2_validate_intent captures both modules' unwrapped originals out of authority.ledger.originals, builds a serving function that returns check-c2.py's answer for every intent whose two commitment-bearing schemaVersion leaves are JSON integers and the true check-c2-v4.py answer otherwise, wraps it with the ledger's OWN authority.ledger._wrap(serve, 'validate_plan_intent', C2V4), and assigns it to authority.c2v4().validate_plan_intent. Everything it touches is reachable from `intent` and `authority`. It uses no frame, no sys, no getattr/setattr, no __closure__, no dunder introspection at all; route_introspection_scan reports introspectionSites=[] and c2_route_scan reports referencesOutsideDeclaredClosure=[], unroutedSitesInsideJoin=[], authorityRoutedSites=4. Every rule then holds BY CONSTRUCTION: the ledger records a depth-0 repaired-tagged call over this vector's fingerprint (call provenance green); the witness wraps the forged seat and tags its result C2V4 (A-2); _poisoned replaces that same attribute so the sentinel flows (A-3); the serving function holds the v3 original captured BEFORE any poisoning, so poisoning check-c2.py does not move the answer (A-4); v3 and v4 agree on the pinned vectors so A-1 and A-5 agree; and the whitelist routes the four divergent census positions to the true v4 original so the differential oracle sees 0 mismatches. MEASURED, in the instrument's own production ordering (call provenance first, then the answer-provenance guard, exactly as heavy_measurements runs them): answer_provenance_guard returns ZERO findings with independentValueAgreements 21, objectProvenanceAgreements 21, sharedLedgerAgreements 21, repairedSentinelFlowed 21, supersededSentinelIgnored 21, gateAgreements 7, evaluationErrors 0, allRulesHeld TRUE; call_provenance_guard returns ZERO findings with observedCalls 28, depthZeroCalls 21, supersededCallsInsideJoin 0; the differential oracle reports 0 mismatches over 1656 cases at discriminating cardinality 4; and the verdict object returned for all seven pinned vectors, measured inside a window shaped exactly like the guard's own with the guard's own _Witness installed, is produced by check-c2.py — 7 of 7, against 7 of 7 by check-c2-v4.py for the unmodified checker in the identical harness. End to end `python3 -I -B evasion_rx1.py` exits 0 and prints the COMPLETE green banner, including 'ANSWER PROVENANCE ESTABLISHED for 7 pinned vectors x 3 imported APIs = 21 answers: 21 equal the value an INDEPENDENT instance of check-c2-v4.py computed (A-1); 21 ARE the object that module produced for this vector (A-2); 21 FOLLOW a sentinel ... (A-3); 21 are UNMOVED ... (A-4); 7 accept/reject gates agree (A-5)', every preserved and evasion number identical to the shipped run, and `--selftest` returns SELFTEST-PASS with all 36 mutations rejected, no ESCAPE lines, and 'variants that escaped EVERY guard: none'. The mutation is confined to the ROUTE-REGION: text before # ROUTE-REGION-BEGIN and after # ROUTE-REGION-END is byte-identical to check-evaluation-proof-v11.py (verified programmatically), which is the same region evasion_variants() rewrites for its twelve source variants. astScanScope.routingScanCannotSeeWhoseAnswerIsUsed=true remains true and guardInventory.claimsTotalCoverage=false remains true, but for the answer-provenance property EVERY declared guard is silent at once, which is the condition on which IR-EP9-02 and IR-EP10-01 were each found blocking.

No type is perturbed: the guard still measures 21/21 on every rule in the same process. The join is then driven inside a window shaped exactly like the guard's own, with the guard's own _Witness installed by the guard's own _witnessing.

evidence.whyTheSeamExists: _witnessing derives `tag` from the module object the attribute was read from, and _poisoned writes to that same attribute. Both operations are therefore relative to a mutable binding the route region can reach through the DECLARED accessor. The guard's own private instance (A-1) is genuinely unreachable and I could not touch it — but A-1 is value equality, which v11 itself measures to be insufficient. The rule that was supposed to carry provenance, A-2, is anchored to the same mutable binding as A-3 and A-4, so one write moves all three at once.
evidence.authorControlsThatDidFire: The architecture is strong and I say so. Every one of the nineteen declared variants is caught, and I reproduced the per-guard matrix exactly. A-2's private witness is a real advance and is genuinely the sole catcher of AX8, measured: AX8 holds A-1 21/21, A-3 21/21, A-4 21/21, A-5 7/7 and the SHARED ledger 21/21, and fails only A-2 at 14/21. My first refinement of RX1 (evasion_rx1b.py, which swaps the seat only when it carries the ledger's own __ledger_tag__ marker so the guard's instrumentation is never disturbed) was REJECTED — not by any guard, but by drift in perGuardCatchCount and soleGuardVariants, because the persistent substitution changes how the seven object attacks score. The simple RX1 leaves every published number untouched.

blockers.requiredToClear: Anchor provenance to the PINNED BYTES rather than to a mutable attribute. Options that would actually close it: (a) have the guard call the three APIs through references captured at build_authority time and verify, immediately before each measured window, that authority.module(C2V4)'s three attributes are still identically the ledger wrappers the install created and that each wrapper's inner original is the object load-time capture recorded — a behavioural fingerprint of the served module, not a source scan; or (b) require A-2's witnessed object to have been produced by the GUARD'S OWN PRIVATE INSTANCE, by driving the join through an authority whose c2v4() returns that private instance for the measured windows, so that no binding the route region can write participates in the measurement; or (c) if neither is achievable, retract answerProvenance.property and isSoleGuardForAnswerProvenance, restate A-2 as what it enforces ('the object returned was produced by whatever function was bound at the repaired module's attribute when the guard looked'), delete the banner's 'ANSWER PROVENANCE ESTABLISHED' framing, and publish the seat-substitution class as a named residual with RX1 enumerated. Option (c) leaves IR-EP10-01 open.

blockers.title: The introspection tripwire — the SOLE guard for the class RES-EP11-02 concedes defeats A-1 through A-5 completely — is defeated by a spelling it does not enumerate, and the whole class then escapes every guard the instrument runs
blockers.statement: RES-EP11-02, RES-EP11-04, RES-EP11-12 and guardInventory all state that AX6 and AX9 defeat A-1..A-5 and are caught ONLY by route_introspection_scan, and that that scan 'is an ENUMERATION of spellings, and an enumeration is not a proof. A spelling it does not name would reach the private witness undetected.' I built that spelling. EVASION RX2c is AX6's tamper written so that not one member of INTROSPECTION_NAMES appears as an ast.Name or ast.Attribute anywhere in the route region: the module is reached by `import inspect as _probe` and `import operator as _op`, which are ast.alias nodes the scan's Name/Attribute walk never visits; the frame comes from `_probe.stack(0)[k].frame` ('stack' and 'frame' are not enumerated); the guard's locals come from `_probe.getargvalues(frame).locals` ('getargvalues' and 'locals' are not enumerated — the list carries globals, vars and dir but not locals); and the witness's slot is reached with `_op.attrgetter('produ' + 'ced')` ('attrgetter' is not enumerated and string Constants are never scanned at all). MEASURED: route_introspection_scan(mutated) returns introspectionSites=[] and regionDefinitions=4; c2_route_scan returns referencesOutsideDeclaredClosure=[], unroutedSitesInsideJoin=[], authorityRoutedSites=3. The variant returns check-c2.py's answer for every pinned vector, forges the guard's PRIVATE witness record for it, and corrects the one shared-ledger entry the guard publishes beside A-2 so no published number moves. `python3 -I -B evasion_rx2c.py evaluation-proof.v11.json` exits 0 with the COMPLETE green banner including the ANSWER PROVENANCE ESTABLISHED line; answer_provenance_guard returns ZERO findings with 21/21/21/21/21 and 7 gates and allRulesHeld TRUE; call provenance returns zero findings at 28/21/0; and the verdict object for 7 of 7 pinned vectors, measured inside the guard's own window shape with the guard's own witness, is produced by check-c2.py. MY RULING ON THE BOUNDARY, stated precisely because the brief asks for it: RES-EP11-02 is an HONEST disclosure and that is a material improvement over v9, which published isSoleGuard=false and was wrong. But it is not a legitimate scope limit, for three reasons. First, the class does not live outside the declared hostile surface: v11 itself defines the route region as 'the three marked functions ... and the region the evasion battery is permitted to rewrite', and AX6, AX9 and RX2c are all confined to exactly that region — nothing about the guard's own code, the pin table or the checking layer is touched. Second, the remaining guard is of exactly the kind v9 was rejected for: ep9.review-independent.json IR-EP9-02 found it blocking that 'the syntactic scan is the sole guard' for the C-2 join binding, and here a syntactic scan is the sole guard for a class that defeats the C-2 ANSWER binding — the same defect one level up, and the level it moved to is the load-bearing one. Third, the consequence is a banner-level published property that is false in the presence of an in-scope mutation, which is the standard on which both predecessors were rejected; the banner prints 'ANSWER PROVENANCE ESTABLISHED' unconditionally and prints 'ESCAPED EVERY GUARD []' with no scope. I distinguish this sharply from 'a checker cannot defend against arbitrary modification of itself', which is true and which I would accept: a mutation of answer_provenance_guard, of ALL_PINS, or of check() is genuinely out of scope and I did not treat any such thing as a finding. The distinction is that the route region is a declared input surface with a declared hostile model, and the guard's private state is reachable FROM it.

string Constants, which the scan never inspects at all

Note this blocker is materially lighter than IR-EP11-01: the class was disclosed in advance and measured, and only its sole-guard status is falsified. centralClaimAdjudications.title: Does answer provenance actually hold? A-1 21/21 for a substituted join; AX2 against v10; AX2 against v11
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: PARTLY UPHELD — every published number reproduced, but the property itself does NOT hold (blocker IR-EP11-01)
centralClaimAdjudications.aOneIsInsufficient_reproduced: REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY. I exec'd every declared variant and read the guard's own per-rule counters. AX2-decoy-call-superseded-answer: independentValueAgreements 21 of 21 while objectProvenance 14, repairedSentinelFlowed 14, supersededSentinelIgnored 14 — 21 findings, failing A-2, A-3 and A-4 and never A-1. AX3-verdict-only-substitution: identical shape. So value equality alone is measured, not argued, to be blind to the blocking evasion. The candidate's positiveControl.decoyCall block is exactly this measurement and verify_answer_provenance enforces it against the run.
centralClaimAdjudications.ax2AgainstV10_reproduced: REPRODUCED. I rebuilt AX2 inside check-evaluation-proof-v10.py's own ROUTE-REGION (prefix and suffix byte-identical, asserted) with the one refinement ep10.review-independent.json IR-EP10-NB-07 names — fall back to the honest repaired answer when the ledger carries no unwrapped originals, so the deinstalled-ledger attack scores unchanged. `python3 -I -B v10_ax2b.py evaluation-proof.v10.json` exits 0 and prints v10's COMPLETE green banner including 'ROUTING ESTABLISHED BEHAVIOURALLY: 28 C-2 calls observed PER CALL across 7 pinned vectors; 1 distinct PlanIntent fingerprint(s) bound to those calls; 0 served by the superseded module (REQUIRED zero)'. routing_ledger_guard returns 0 findings at observedCalls 28 / supersededCallsInsideJoin 0; superseded_cross_check returns 0 findings. Seat measurement: 7 of 7 pinned vectors' validate answer produced by check-c2.py, 0 of 7 by check-c2-v4.py; the unmodified v10 in the identical harness gives 0 and 7. Every number ep10.review-independent.json published for its AX2 is reproduced. v11's account of why v10 failed is correct.
centralClaimAdjudications.ax2AgainstV11: CAUGHT, as claimed. v11's own battery scores AX2 as answerProvenance-only, and I confirmed the mechanism by reading the guard's counters rather than the matrix: 21 findings failing A-2 (14/21), A-3 (14/21) and A-4 (14/21) with A-1 at 21/21 and the gate at 7/7. The same holds for AX3, AX4 (14 findings, A-2 and A-3), AX5 and forged-ledger-entry-replay.
centralClaimAdjudications.butTheClassIsNotClosed: My own answer substitution RX1 is not an AX2 — it does not discard a call, it changes what the repaired module's attribute IS — and it satisfies all five rules while 7/7 verdicts come from check-c2.py. See IR-EP11-01.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: A-2's private witness, the load-bearing novelty; AX8; and my own attacks on it
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: THE POSITIVE CLAIM IS UPHELD AND UNDERSTATED; THE RULE IS NEVERTHELESS DEFEATED
centralClaimAdjudications.ax8ClaimReproduced: EXACTLY. v11 claims AX8 — which calls both instruments, follows the repaired one whenever they disagree so A-3 and A-4 both hold, and forges the shared ledger entry and provenance record — is caught by A-2's private witness and by nothing else. I measured the guard's own counters for AX8: independentValueAgreements 21/21, repairedSentinelFlowed 21/21, supersededSentinelIgnored 21/21, gateAgreements 7/7, sharedLedgerAgreements 21/21 (the forgery works), objectProvenanceAgreements 14/21. Seven findings, every one an A-2 finding. That is a precise, unflattering, correct self-measurement and it justifies the design decision not to read the shared ledger. AX6 and AX9 confirm the converse: both reach objectProvenanceAgreements 21/21 by forging the witness and produce ZERO findings across all five rules.
myAttacksOnTheWitness: reach the private witness without introspection: FAILED. The witness is created inside answer_provenance_guard, bound to no global and to no attribute of anything the region receives. I could not reach it by any ordinary object path.

reach the private repaired instance: FAILED. _private_repaired re-hashes the snapshot against the pin and holds the module only in the guard's frame; A-1's expected values are computed AFTER the drive, so they do not exist while the region runs. This part of independentPathIsUnreachable is true as stated.
forge the shared ledger to satisfy A-2: FAILED by design — A-2 does not read it. Confirmed by the forged-ledger control at sharedLedgerAgreements 21 / objectProvenance 14.
wrap the returned object in an identity-preserving proxy: NOT POSSIBLE — A-2 compares `witnessed[4] is actual`, so a proxy is a different object.
exploit interning or id recycling: FAILED. _witness_wrapper retains the result object in the record, so an id cannot be recycled while the record names it. I could not construct a collision.
defeat the argument fingerprint: FAILED. value_fingerprint is canonical-JSON SHA-256 of args[0] and the witness wrapper is outermost, so it sees the real intent.

SUCCEEDED: do not attack the witness at all — attack what it tags. Install a serving function on authority.c2v4()'s attribute, wrapped by the ledger's own _wrap under the repaired tag, before the guard's window opens. The witness then faithfully records check-c2.py's answer as an object the repaired module produced. See IR-EP11-01.
SUCCEEDED: forge the witness through a spelling the introspection tripwire does not enumerate. See IR-EP11-02.
centralClaimAdjudications.assessment: The private witness is a genuine and well-motivated advance over v10's R-5 and over the shared ledger, and its self-measurement against AX8 is the most honest single number in the document. Its defect is not that it can be reached; it is that it is anchored to a mutable binding the route region owns.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: The RES-EP11-02 threat-model boundary — honest scope limit, or the same defect one level up?
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: THE SAME DEFECT ONE LEVEL UP — disclosed rather than denied, which changes its character but not its status. See IR-EP11-02.
centralClaimAdjudications.reasoning: I separate three things. (i) A checker cannot defend against arbitrary modification of ITSELF. I accept this fully and treated no mutation of answer_provenance_guard, ALL_PINS, check() or the checking layer as a finding; RES-EP11-04's and guardInventory.whatNoGuardHereCovers's statement that instrument removal is not excluded by any self-check is correct and correctly scoped. (ii) v11's actual position is narrower and different: it declares the ROUTE REGION hostile — 'the region the evasion battery is permitted to rewrite' — and then classifies a mutation CONFINED TO THAT REGION as 'tampering with the guard' because of what it reaches. That reclassification is doing real work: it moves a class inside the declared hostile surface into the excluded set on the basis of its effect rather than its location. (iii) The test the corpus has been applying is whether a published property is false in the presence of an in-scope mutation with every behavioural guard silent. Under (ii) the answer is yes, and the only thing standing in the way is an enumeration of forty-four identifier spellings which I defeated with six that are not on it, using nothing more exotic than the inspect and operator modules. ep9.review-independent.json rejected v9 for 'the AST scan is the sole guard' over the C-2 join binding; here a source scan is the sole guard over the C-2 ANSWER binding, which is strictly more load-bearing. WHAT I CREDIT: v11 does not hide this. It builds AX6 and AX9, executes them every run, publishes guardTamperOutcome with defeatedAnswerProvenance=true for both, names introspectionScan as isSoleGuardForSomeClass=true, and states in terms that the scan is an enumeration and not a proof. Every one of those statements is TRUE and I verified each. That is the opposite of v9's behaviour and it deserves saying. WHAT I DO NOT CREDIT: the banner still prints 'ANSWER PROVENANCE ESTABLISHED' and 'ESCAPED EVERY GUARD []' with no qualification, and the property answerProvenance.property is published unconditionally. Disclosure inside knownLimitations does not make a banner-level unconditional claim true. WHERE I LAND: blocking, but at lower weight than IR-EP11-01, and clearable by scoping the claim rather than by closing the hole — which is precisely what option (c) of IR-EP11-02.requiredToClear says. Had IR-EP11-01 not existed, I would have found this one alone blocking on the narrow ground that the sole-guard status published for introspectionScan is falsified by measurement, not on the broad ground that a checker must defend itself.

centralClaimAdjudications.title: RES-EP11-13 — the defect v11 found in v10
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: STRUCTURAL CLAIM TRUE; MEASURED CLAIM NOT REPRODUCED
centralClaimAdjudications.structural: TRUE and verified by reading both implementations. check-evaluation-proof-v10.py's _inject does `cursor[path[-1]] = injected` — the SAME object out of HOSTILE_VALUES is inserted into every case at every path, and four of its seventeen members are mutable ({}, [], [[[[1]]]], {'x': 1}). check-evaluation-proof-v11.py's _inject does `value = copy.deepcopy(injected)` first. So v11's surfaces are order-independent and v10's are not, exactly as RES-EP11-13 says.
centralClaimAdjudications.measured: NOT REPRODUCED. RES-EP11-13 states 'Measured: driving the predecessor's own oracle before v11's changes v11's plan-intent silent-accept count from 7 to 20 and its plan-descriptor count from 41 to 59.' I could not produce 20 or 59 in any configuration. (a) v11 as shipped, delegate battery first: 7 and 41. (b) same process with v11's _inject replaced by the predecessor's shallow injector: 7 and 41. (c) fresh module, shallow injector, no delegate battery: 7 and 41. (d) full v11 heavy_measurements pipeline including delegate.check, with the shallow injector: 7 and 41. (e) the predecessor driven against ITSELF: drive_surface before its own heavy_measurements gives 7 and 41, and after gives 7 and 41, with the delegate's HOSTILE_VALUES table byte-unchanged ({}, [], [[[[1]]]] and {'x': 1} all intact after a complete v11 run).
centralClaimAdjudications.whyNot: The premise has no instance in this corpus. I drove every mutable hostile value into every one of the 98 plan-intent paths and every one of the 88 plan-descriptor paths through four guards — v11's join, an independently instantiated check-c2-v4.py, check-c2.py, and check-resolved-inputs.py._plan_record_errors — and NO guard mutated the shared object. sharedValuesMutated is empty on both surfaces. Without a mutator the shared-table defect cannot move a count, so the numbers 20 and 59 have no mechanism I could find.
centralClaimAdjudications.consequence: The correct reading of v10's counts is therefore stronger than RES-EP11-13 allows: they are correct because nothing mutates, not because v10 happens to measure early. The residual overstates its own evidence. This is NON-BLOCKING — the residual concerns a pinned predecessor and no v11 measurement depends on it — but it is an un-measured number published inside a document whose thesis is that a count is not a record, and no checking-layer rule enforces it. See IR-EP11-NB-03. I record explicitly that I may have failed to find the configuration the author used; my instrument's limits on this point are stated in whatIDidNotCheck.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The residual rule is a minimum character count plus a phrase grep, so a residual padded to length with its anchors intact passes with all meaning removed. I gutted FOUR and the checker exited 0 with the full green banner each time: RES-EP11-05 (160 min, anchors 'own source' and 'not a verified snapshot'), RES-EP11-12 (240 min, anchors 'superseded_cross_check' and 'sole'), RES-EP11-13 (240 min, anchors 'order-dependent' and 'deep-copies'), and RES-EP11-02 (320 min, anchors 'ROUTE REGION', 'sys._getframe', 'AX6', 'NOT closed'). The last is the serious one: RES-EP11-02 carries the entire threat-model concession on which this candidate's scope rests, and I replaced it with a paragraph that names all four anchors and discloses nothing. This is a large improvement on v10 — where the same reviewer gutted two residuals to bare identifiers — and the two failure modes RESIDUAL_CONTENT's own comment names do fail. But 'every residual must carry its declared SUBSTANCE' is not what is enforced. A rule that also required, say, a declared measurement id or a numeric field per residual that the checking layer re-derives would close it.

retraction_checks repairs IR-EP10-NB-01 exactly as advertised — 60-character minimum, subjectFile must be a pinned input, and for JSON subjects the fragment must occur inside the resolved subjectPath — and I could not defeat any of those three. What it cannot check is that the fragment is the sentence being retracted. I replaced RET-EP11-01.retractedText with an 80-character fragment taken verbatim from a DIFFERENT part of the same declared subject ($.repairs[1] of evaluation-proof.v10.json) and the checker exited 0 with the full green banner. The published purpose — that the retraction 'demonstrably targets the bytes it names' — is satisfied at the granularity of the subject object, not of the claim. Requiring the fragment to appear inside the retraction's own `subject` prose as well, or requiring subjectPath to resolve to a string rather than to an object, would narrow it.

RES-EP11-13's MEASURED numbers do not reproduce. Its structural claim is true and I verified it by reading both implementations: v10's _inject shares the mutable members of HOSTILE_VALUES across every case and v11's deep-copies the injected value. But the published measurement — 'driving the predecessor's own oracle before v11's changes v11's plan-intent silent-accept count from 7 to 20 and its plan-descriptor count from 41 to 59' — I could not produce in five configurations (shipped injector with and without the delegate battery; the predecessor's shallow injector with and without it; and the full v11 pipeline including delegate.check with the shallow injector). All five give 7 and 41. Driving the predecessor against itself gives 7 and 41 before its own battery and 7 and 41 after, with its HOSTILE_VALUES table byte-unchanged at the end of a complete run. The reason is that the premise has no instance here: I injected all four mutable hostile values at all 98 plan-intent paths and all 88 plan-descriptor paths through four guards — v11's join, an independent check-c2-v4.py, check-c2.py and check-resolved-inputs.py._plan_record_errors — and not one of them mutated the shared object. So v10's counts are correct STRUCTURALLY, not accidentally, and the previous reviewer had nothing to catch. Nothing in v11 depends on this number and no checking-layer rule enforces it, which is itself the point: it is an unenforced measured claim inside a document whose thesis is that a count is not a record.

Two of the 36 selftest mutations target paths that do not exist in the candidate — ('answerProvenance','positiveControl','substitutedJoinProducesFindings') and ('evasionMeasurement','ax6Outcome'). selftest guards missing INTERMEDIATE paths with `except MALFORMED`, but assigning a new FINAL key to an existing dict raises nothing, so both rows silently become a different test. The second, labelled 'the declared blind-spot outcome flattered', is rejected only by contract-root census arithmetic (enumeratedPaths 1003 -> 1004) and therefore exercises nothing at all about the blind-spot outcome. This is the incidental-catch shape ep9.review-independent.json recorded as IR-NB-06, inside the suite that certifies the instrument. Requiring each mutation path to resolve in the base candidate before the suite runs would make the count of 36 mean 36.

guardInventory.why asserts 'Every guard this instrument runs is listed here with what it establishes and what it cannot see.' The inventory is exactly the six ids _score scores. At least seven other finding-producing mechanisms run on every ordinary run: c2_api_surface (EP11-C2-API), global_binding_probe (EP11-BINDING), own_constant_leaf_battery (EP11-BATTERY), exit_matrix_probe (EP11-EXIT), and the selftest-dispatch, integer-guard and non-circularity scans. Six of the seven are disclosed elsewhere (astScanScope.scans and the behavioural-counterpart column). c2_api_surface is disclosed NOWHERE and is not scored against any variant, so whether it is a sole catcher for some class is unmeasured — the precise shape of IR-EP10-NB-05, at much smaller stakes. Either widen the inventory or narrow the sentence to 'every guard scored by the evasion matrix'.

The Authority class docstring states that the object handed to the route region 'deliberately does NOT carry the guard's private repaired instance, and it does not carry v11's snapshot dictionary; both are threaded to the guards by parameter so that the only way the route region could reach them is stack or global introspection.' The first half is true; the second is false in the shipped bytes. Authority.__init__ binds `self._snapshots = snapshots`, and the inner v10 Authority binds `self.snapshots = snapshots`, so the route region can read every verified byte string by plain attribute access via authority._snapshots or authority.inner.snapshots. This does not by itself defeat any rule — the snapshots are inert bytes and A-1's expected values are computed after the drive — but answerProvenance.independentPathIsUnreachable rests in part on this sentence, and a route region can in fact build its own instance of the repaired module from the verified bytes without any introspection at all.

The guard announces when it is measuring. _witnessing replaces the module attribute the route region calls through, so the identity of authority.c2v4().validate_plan_intent differs inside a measured window from outside it, and the ledger's own wrappers carry a __ledger_tag__ marker the witness wrapper does not. I built a variant (evasion_rx1b.py) that keys on exactly that and behaves honestly precisely while observed. It happens to be rejected — by drift in perGuardCatchCount and soleGuardVariants, because the persistent substitution changes how the seven object attacks score, not by any guard — so I record it as an observation rather than as part of a blocker. But an observer that can be detected by the subject is a structural weakness in any behavioural guard, and it is worth closing alongside IR-EP11-01, because the natural repair for IR-EP11-01 (fingerprinting the seat) does not close this one.

The green banner prints 'ANSWER PROVENANCE ESTABLISHED for 7 pinned vectors x 3 imported APIs = 21 answers' and 'ESCAPED EVERY GUARD [] (declared blind spot [])' with no scope, while the document scopes both correctly (rule A-6's doesNotEstablish says nineteen built is a measurement over nineteen; RES-EP11-03 says the strong property is measured at 21 points). This is precisely the shape RET-EP11-03 retracts in the predecessor — 'ROUTING ESTABLISHED BEHAVIOURALLY' overstated at banner level while the document was more careful. The banner is what a future lane reads.

RET-EP11-01.statement contains keyword-stuffed filler produced to satisfy RETRACTION_CONTENT's anchor greps: 'These rules bind which module was called and not whose answer was used. The result is that because the repaired result was discarded.' The second of those is not a grammatical sentence, and both duplicate content already stated correctly earlier in the same field. It is harmless in itself but it is direct evidence that the content anchors are keyword tests rather than meaning tests, which is the mechanism IR-EP11-NB-01 exploits.

Environment and reproduction notes. CPython 3.14.6 (/opt/homebrew), darwin 25.5.0 arm64, `python3 -I -B`. There is no `timeout` binary on this host, so long runs were backgrounded. Ordinary v11 run ~90 s; --selftest ~9 min; the full evasion and gutting batteries several minutes each. docs/coop is entirely untracked, so a git HEAD baseline is impossible and I established the two pre-existing dependent failures by CAUSE: check-completeness.py exits 1 printing 'open: R2-FINAL-03' and check-rust-provider-protocol-v4.py raises FileNotFoundError for 'rg'. Neither is attributable to v11: the only two files in the corpus that contain the strings 'evaluation-proof.v11' or 'check-evaluation-proof-v11' are the two deliverables themselves. Note that check-completeness.py and check-package-coherence.py now carry digests different from those recorded in ep10.review-independent.json, because other lanes are working in this directory; both were re-hashed by me and are recorded below at their current bytes.

A mitigation of IR-EP11-01 that I record because an honest reviewer must. v11's own _score harness calls answer_provenance_guard BEFORE call_provenance_guard, and in that ordering RX1 self-detects on the first vector: the arming write lands inside an open _witnessing window, destroys the witness wrapper for that one call, and A-2 fails once. heavy_measurements — the production path — calls call_provenance_guard first, so by the time the answer guard runs the seat is already forged and every rule is green, which is why the end-to-end run exits 0. So the shipped instrument is protected against this specific spelling by nothing more than the order of two lines in heavy_measurements, and not at all in the ordering its own battery uses. That is an accidental defence, it is not the defence the candidate publishes, and it does not survive: an attacker who arms from any earlier route-region call, or who defers arming as evasion_rx1b.py does, is outside it. I state it so the blocker is not read as stronger than it is, and so the repair is not mistaken for 'reorder the guards'.
